FIB_PLUS	<p>80b4_e04d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3044;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9f3044;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3044;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #50680e;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #50680e;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #50680e;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4952b4;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4952b4;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4952b4;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mpt, +++, mpt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3044;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9f3044;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3044;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #50680e;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #50680e;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #50680e;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668e;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00668e;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668e;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fjr, +++, fjr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e19;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #874e19;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e19;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1a6978;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1a6978;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1a6978;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6d41b2;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6d41b2;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d41b2;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, etx, +++, etx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #50680e;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #50680e;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #50680e;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1a6978;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1a6978;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1a6978;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6d41b2;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6d41b2;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d41b2;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mwx, +++, mwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f23;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #973f23;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f23;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c69;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c69;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c69;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4952b4;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4952b4;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4952b4;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, krx, +++, krx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7b5601;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315f9a;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #315f9a;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315f9a;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #96326e;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #96326e;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #96326e;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bch, +++, bch"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>fb08_2575</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f23;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #973f23;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f23;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #50680e;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #50680e;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #50680e;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315f9a;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #315f9a;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315f9a;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aew, +++, aew"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f23;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #973f23;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f23;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e35;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2c6e35;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e35;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315f9a;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #315f9a;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #315f9a;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, etx, +++, etx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7b5601;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e53;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e53;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e53;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #315f9a;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #315f9a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>ae71_d6d6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3044;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9f3044;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3044;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #695f0c;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #695f0c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f0c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4952b4;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4952b4;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3044;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9f3044;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3044;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #50680e;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #50680e;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #50680e;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1a6978;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1a6978;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f23;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #973f23;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f23;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c69;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c69;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c69;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6d41b2;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6d41b2;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d41b2;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfk, +++, cfk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>00b5_eb42</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #50680e;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #50680e;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #50680e;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1a6978;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1a6978;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1a6978;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6d41b2;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6d41b2;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>b3e2_08bb</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f0c;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #695f0c;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f0c;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c69;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c69;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c69;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873695;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #873695;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e19;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #874e19;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e19;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e35;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2c6e35;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e35;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4952b4;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4952b4;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f23;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #973f23;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f23;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e53;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e53;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e53;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4952b4;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4952b4;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3044;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9f3044;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3044;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e35;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #2c6e35;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e35;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668e;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00668e;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7b5601;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c69;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c69;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c69;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873695;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #873695;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". FIB_PLUS	<p>84f3_fc1e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7b5601;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1a6978;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1a6978;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1a6978;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873695;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #873695;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. whole number. FIB_PLUS	<p>35b4_7df7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7b5601;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c69;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c69;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c69;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873695;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #873695;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #873695;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, efh, +++, efh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e35;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2c6e35;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e35;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668e;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00668e;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668e;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873695;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #873695;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7b5601;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5601;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668e;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00668e;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668e;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #96326e;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #96326e;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #96326e;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bnw, +++, bnw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>a2f6_7bbc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e19;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #874e19;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e19;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c69;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c69;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c69;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #873695;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #873695;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #873695;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cmt, +++, cmt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f0c;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #695f0c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f0c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c69;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c69;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c69;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4952b4;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4952b4;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype.
